title: Quentin and the Wolf
premise: Paloma Thackeray steals memories for coin, slipping along smuggler roads no one else can navigate — until a client's ledger reveals her in a century-old prophecy, named as the thief who will unbind the Wolf-King of Thornfell. Hunted by the crown's memory-eaters and guided by Quentin, the exiled heir whose mind the Wolf has half-consumed, she must gather the scattered memories of the true king before the Wolf devours what remains. In the end Paloma learns the prophecy was written by her own grandmother as a trap for the Wolf, and she chooses to give up her stolen hoard — including her own childhood — to rebind it, finding family not in blood but in those who remember her anyway.
about_author: Ansel Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a mountain border town before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who carry other people's pasts.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She lifts a memory from a merchant on the Salt Stair road, showing her craft and her rule: never keep what you steal. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking hunger for connection.

chapters.title: A Client with Cold Hands
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A pale stranger hires her to retrieve a sealed memory-vial from a Thornfell vault, paying in old royal coin. Beat: unease beneath greed; the coin bears the Wolf sigil.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Knew Her Name
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Inside the vault she finds a prophetic ledger written in 1800s script naming 'the Thackeray thief' and tonight's date. Beat: vertigo — her life already written.

chapters.title: Quentin at the Crossroads
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The exiled heir intercepts her on the smuggler road, recognizing the ledger's seal. He is gaunt, half-hollowed, hearing the Wolf in his skull. Beat: wary alliance born of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Wears
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He explains the usurper king is the Wolf wearing his father's crown and face, feeding on royal memory to hold its shape. Beat: horror and grief for a father he cannot mourn.

chapters.title: Memory-Eaters on the Pass
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Crown hunters attack; Paloma escapes using a stolen memory of the pass that isn't hers, nearly losing herself inside it. Beat: first cost of her gift.

chapters.title: The Hoard Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Quentin leads her to his hidden cache of the true king's scattered memories. Beat: tentative trust; Paloma recognizes her grandmother's handwriting on the seals.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Trap
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She deciphers the ledger: her grandmother wrote the prophecy as a binding ritual requiring a Thackeray thief. Beat: fury and awe — she was raised as an instrument.

chapters.title: The Inn of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sheltering with found-family smugglers who once served his mother, Quentin tastes belonging he never had at court. Beat: warmth; Paloma watches him have what she never did.

chapters.title: The Vial Opens
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Curiosity wins; she opens the client's vial and receives the king's final living memory — the moment the Wolf took him. Beat: trauma shared across a century.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Ford
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Ambush at the river; a memory-eater tears Quentin's childhood name from him. Beat: loss — he forgets his mother's face.

chapters.title: I'll Remember For You
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She carries Quentin's lost memory alongside her own, promising to give it back. Beat: the thief becomes keeper; tenderness neither names.

chapters.title: The City of the Usurper
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They infiltrate the capital during a festival of forgetting. Beat: dread dressed in celebration; the crowd smiles with empty eyes.

chapters.title: Court of Hollow Faces
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin walks his own palace unrecognized; courtiers he loved greet him as a stranger. Beat: exile made flesh.

chapters.title: The Wolf's Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Wolf-king offers her anything — including her erased childhood — if she delivers Quentin. Beat: temptation that knows her exactly.

chapters.title: Refusal and Ruin
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin refuses for her; they flee the palace through burning gardens. Beat: loyalty chosen over salvation.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Old contacts shelter them, but one sells their route to the crown. Betrayal beat: the loneliness she always feared, confirmed.

chapters.title: What Paloma Stole First
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin discovers her earliest theft was her own painful childhood — she erased herself long ago. Beat: understanding; her emptiness has an origin.

chapters.title: The Mountain That Remembers
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They reach the prophecy's site: a shrine where stone holds memory like wax. Beat: reverent dread; the trap begins to close.

chapters.title: Ritual of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following grandmother's instructions, Paloma begins the unbinding rite — which requires a willing king's memory as anchor. Beat: dawning cost.

chapters.title: Quentin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin offers his remaining self as the anchor. Paloma refuses to spend him. Beat: love argued as arithmetic; both lose the argument.

chapters.title: The Wolf Descends
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The Wolf arrives in full power, wearing the king's face, offering mercy with teeth. Beat: terror; the mountain shakes.

chapters.title: Half a King
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin fights the Wolf inside his own mind while Paloma works the rite outside. Beat: interior battle rendered as a house burning room by room.

chapters.title: The Thief's Choice
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The rite demands a hoard of stolen memory equal to a kingdom's worth. Only her lifetime collection qualifies. Beat: sacrifice crystallizes.

chapters.title: Everything I Ever Took
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She pours her hoard into the binding — every stolen sunset, every borrowed grief. Beat: elegiac release; becoming empty on purpose.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The Wolf is torn from the crown; the true king's memory rises whole for one breath. Beat: triumph shadowed by Paloma collapsing, hollowed.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin holds the amnesiac Paloma, returning her kept memories one by one — except her own childhood, gone forever. Beat: grief and gratitude entwined.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Without a King
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The restored memory names Quentin heir, but the court fears him. Beat: inheritance as burden; he hesitates at the throne.

chapters.title: The Stranger in My House
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Recovering among the smugglers, Paloma meets Quentin again without knowing why her chest aches. Beat: bittersweet comedy of almost-recognition.

chapters.title: Remembering Forward
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Quentin tells her their story nightly; she falls for him twice. Beat: found family rebuilt around absence.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Last Page
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A hidden ledger page reveals grandmother erased herself the same way — and left a message: 'what you give, the mountain keeps.' Beat: lineage of sacrifice understood.

chapters.title: The Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the shrine, the stone returns fragments: her grandmother's voice, then a single memory of young Paloma. Beat: hope kindled carefully.

chapters.title: Coronation of the Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin accepts the crown only if the smugglers stand beside him. Beat: found family elevated to court; the hollow faces begin to fill.

chapters.title: The Memory-Eaters' End
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma dismantles the crown's memory-eater order, freeing stored memories back to the people. Beat: righteous reckoning; her skills turned to restoration.

chapters.title: What Was Never Stolen
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin gives Paloma new first memories — a festival, a snowfall, deliberately made together. Beat: joy authored rather than inherited.

chapters.title: The Wolf's Whisper
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A fragment of the Wolf survived in the shrine stone, whispering to the desperate. Beat: sequel-shadow tension; evil endures in small hungers.

chapters.title: Rebinding the Stone
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Together they complete grandmother's true design: not destroying the Wolf but teaching the mountain to digest it. Beat: partnership perfected; the trap finally sprung.

chapters.title: Thackeray Road
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The smuggler roads are renamed for her; she maps them anew, keeping nothing, giving freely. Beat: identity remade — a keeper, not a thief.

chapters.title: The Family We Made
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A quiet chapter: the inn, the smugglers, the courtiers, one table. Beat: fullness after hunger; belonging earned.

chapters.title: Quentin and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma writes their story into a new ledger so no prophecy will ever surprise them again — ending with the line that began the book. Beat: circular closure; memory chosen over fate.
